scenes.tts: If a protein is enough to start making a motor neuron, does every motor neuron need it?
scenes.visual: Title card: Enough, Needed, and Kept. Two words on screen: enough? needed?
scenes.narration: If a protein is enough to start making a motor neuron, does every motor neuron need it?

scenes.tts: A factor is sufficient if adding it produces the effect, in the cells being tested.
scenes.visual: Definition card: sufficient = adding it produces the effect, in the cells tested.
scenes.narration: A factor is sufficient if adding it produces the effect, in the cells being tested.

scenes.tts: It is necessary there if the effect does not happen without it.
scenes.visual: Definition card: necessary = without it, the effect fails, in the cells tested.
scenes.narration: It is necessary there if the effect does not happen without it.

scenes.tts: Electroporation in chick tests sufficiency. Gene deletion in mouse tests necessity.
scenes.visual: Split screen. Left: a chick neural tube in section, one side turned green by an electric pulse, the other side labelled control; label: electroporation tests sufficiency. Right: a mouse embryo icon with a gene crossed out; label: deletion tests necessity.
scenes.narration: Electroporation in chick tests sufficiency. Gene deletion in mouse tests necessity.

scenes.tts: In chick, M N X one, or its relative M N R two, is enough to trigger motor neuron differentiation.
scenes.caption: In chick, Mnx1, or its relative MNR2, is enough to trigger motor-neuron differentiation.
scenes.visual: Electroporated side of the chick cord: Mnx1 (or chick MNR2) added; motor-neuron markers appear.
scenes.narration: In chick, Mnx1, or its relative MNR2, is enough to trigger motor-neuron differentiation.

scenes.tts: It also represses the neighbouring V two programme.
scenes.caption: It also represses the neighbouring V2 programme.
scenes.visual: On the same side, V2 genes dim with a down arrow.
scenes.narration: It also represses the neighbouring V2 programme.

scenes.tts: Predict. Delete M N X one in a mouse. Are motor neurons made? Does anything go wrong?
scenes.caption: Predict. Delete Mnx1 in a mouse. Are motor neurons made? Does anything go wrong?
scenes.visual: Question card over a mouse cord section with Mnx1 crossed out: made? anything wrong?
scenes.narration: Predict. Delete Mnx1 in a mouse. Are motor neurons made? Does anything go wrong?

scenes.tts: They are made, on schedule and in normal numbers.
scenes.visual: The mouse cord section fills with motor neurons in their usual place. Label: on schedule, normal numbers.
scenes.narration: They are made, on schedule and in normal numbers.

scenes.tts: But for a while they show V two interneuron features. Their columns and axon paths are disordered.
scenes.caption: But for a while they show V2 interneuron features. Their columns and axon paths are disordered.
scenes.visual: Some motor neurons flicker with the V2 colour (Chx10). The columns blur and axons leave on tangled paths. Credit: Arber et al. and Thaler et al., 1999.
scenes.narration: But for a while they show V2 interneuron features. Their columns and axon paths are disordered.

scenes.tts: So M N X one is not needed to make a motor neuron. It is needed to keep one.
scenes.caption: So Mnx1 is not needed to make a motor neuron. It is needed to keep one.
scenes.visual: Two labels: make (no), keep (yes) beside Mnx1.
scenes.narration: So Mnx1 is not needed to make a motor neuron. It is needed to keep one.

scenes.tts: A motor neuron has to keep suppressing the interneuron programme. That is the lock.
scenes.visual: The padlock from chapter 1 closes over the motor-neuron cell; the V2 genes stay dim.
scenes.narration: A motor neuron has to keep suppressing the interneuron programme. That is the lock.

scenes.tts: Back up to the progenitors. Delete both Olig one and Olig two, and motor neurons are largely lost.
scenes.caption: Back up to the progenitors. Delete both Olig1 and Olig2, and motor neurons are largely lost.
scenes.visual: Genotype table, row 1 builds: Olig1 and Olig2 deleted; motor neurons made? largely no.
scenes.narration: Back up to the progenitors. Delete both Olig1 and Olig2, and motor neurons are largely lost.

scenes.tts: Lineage tracing suggested the progenitors make V two interneurons, then astrocytes, instead.
scenes.caption: Lineage tracing suggested the progenitors make V2 interneurons, then astrocytes, instead.
scenes.visual: Row 1 completes: pMN cells make V2 interneurons, then astrocytes (lineage tracing suggested); no oligodendrocytes. Label: acts in progenitors.
scenes.narration: Lineage tracing suggested the progenitors make V2 interneurons, then astrocytes, instead.

scenes.tts: Delete Islet one, and motor neurons are not generated at all.
scenes.caption: Delete Isl1, and motor neurons are not generated at all.
scenes.visual: Row 2 builds: Isl1 deleted; motor neurons made? no; Engrailed1 interneurons also fail. Credit: Pfaff et al., 1996.
scenes.narration: Delete Isl1, and motor neurons are not generated at all.

scenes.tts: Now a puzzle. Delete L H X three and L H X four. Motor neurons are still made.
scenes.caption: Now a puzzle. Delete Lhx3 and Lhx4. Motor neurons are still made.
scenes.visual: Row 4 builds: Lhx3 and Lhx4 deleted; motor neurons made? yes.
scenes.narration: Now a puzzle. Delete Lhx3 and Lhx4. Motor neurons are still made.

scenes.tts: What changes is their subclass, and which way their axons leave the tube.
scenes.visual: Row 4 completes: subclass and axon exit change. Axons in the section leave by a different route.
scenes.narration: What changes is their subclass, and which way their axons leave the tube.

scenes.tts: Yet L H X three sits in the motor neuron complex. How can both be true?
scenes.caption: Yet Lhx3 sits in the motor-neuron complex. How can both be true?
scenes.visual: The chapter 1 motor-neuron complex beside row 4, with a question mark between them.
scenes.narration: Yet Lhx3 sits in the motor-neuron complex. How can both be true?

scenes.tts: The tests ask different questions. In chick, Islet one plus L H X three is enough to start the programme.
scenes.caption: The tests ask different questions. In chick, Isl1 plus Lhx3 is enough to start the programme.
scenes.visual: Split screen: chick, labelled sufficient (Isl1 plus Lhx3 starts the programme); mouse, labelled necessary.
scenes.narration: The tests ask different questions. In chick, Isl1 plus Lhx3 is enough to start the programme.

scenes.tts: In mouse, motor neurons still form without L H X three and four, but of a different kind. Sufficient is not the same as necessary.
scenes.visual: Mouse side: the double mutant, Lhx3 and Lhx4 deleted. The cells are still motor neurons, of a different kind, and their axons leave by a different route. Label: sufficient is not necessary.
scenes.narration: In mouse, motor neurons still form without Lhx3 and Lhx4, but of a different kind. Sufficient is not the same as necessary.
scenes.caption: In mouse, motor neurons still form without Lhx3 and Lhx4, but of a different kind. Sufficient is not the same as necessary.

scenes.tts: Takeaway: enough, needed, and kept are different jobs. Each test answers only one.
scenes.visual: Closing card: enough, needed, kept, three jobs.
scenes.narration: Takeaway: enough, needed, and kept are different jobs. Each test answers only one.
